channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Google agrees to share app catalogue in new Epic settlement
item.description: Google and Epic Games have restructured their settlement proposal in an attempt to appease concerns that their prior agreement upended key aspects of the permanent injunction issued by the US District Court for the Northern District of California.

item.title: Ticketmaster used Live Nation ties for “threats”, arena execs say
item.description: A Ticketmaster executive made “credible threats” that Live Nation would withhold concerts from a venue in Minnesota if it used a rival’s ticketing platform, a witness called by the Department of Justice has alleged.

item.title: Brace for it: The Briefing for 5 March 2026
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority is not afraid of the dentist’s chair. Announcing a market study into the private dentistry sector today, the agency plans to shine a light on any potentially anticompetitive practices relating to availability, choice and prices. Also in The Briefing, a novel class action against six water utility companies sinks on appeal, the CMA accepts failing firm arg...

item.title: Hong Kong enforcer suffers rare loss in hotel cartel case
item.description: Hong Kong’s Competition Tribunal has refused to fine a local hotel for allegedly facilitating a price-fixing scheme because the territory’s antitrust watchdog brought the case based on an incorrect interpretation of the law.

item.title: Loriot: Price effects still a priority for EU merger enforcement
item.description: The “bread and butter” issue of price effects should remain a key focus of the European Commission’s deal reviews despite a push to introduce other considerations, according to the agency’s deputy director-general for mergers.

item.title: ACM open to testing “creative” divestment guarantees for efficiency arguments
item.description: The head of the Netherlands Authority for Consumer and Markets has suggested exploring mandatory divestments should promised efficiencies fail to materialise following merger reviews.

item.title: Google loses landmark constitutional challenge in Canadian adtech probe
item.description: Google has failed to convince Canada’s Competition Tribunal that the country’s antitrust watchdog breached its constitutional rights by exposing it to a potential record penalty.

item.title: Everybody’s a critic: The Tipline for 5 March 2026
item.description: Federal and state enforcers may not be the only US obstacles for Paramount/Warner Bros Discovery. item.title: Live Nation tours a necessity, DC concert operator says
item.description: An independent concert operator has testified that he was “concerned” about booking enough concerts to survive without Live Nation.

item.title: Dems propose extraordinary meatpacking divestitures
item.description: Senate Democrats have introduced legislation that would require the Federal Trade Commission to break up the largest meatpacking conglomerates by establishing bright-line rules against vertical integration and concentration.
